newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds dash higher but cap seen around 101.10/20.
newsitem.headline: Bunds dash higher but cap seen around 101.10/20.

text.p: German Bund futures made a lively start to Thursday's session, dashing up to take on a small resistance barrier at the previous day's high of 101.01.
With heavy volumes in the first few minutes of trade, dealers said the market was evidently relieved to have the opportunity to push higher.
"It is very lively here this morning. We have already traded around 14,000 contracts on the DTB so far," said one trader at Deutsche Bank futures and options in Frankfurt.
By 0649 GMT, the DTB June contract was 33 basis points higher at 101.00, afer earlier touching a high at 101.07.
February retail sales data showed a nominal decline of 5.0 percent on the year and a real decline of 6.0 percent.
"Most houses didn't expect them to be as weak as that, so that is obviously supporting the market in its bid to push to the upside," said the trader.

While analysts said momentum signals were positive, they said the June DTB Bund would probably run into difficulties at around 101.13, where the 50 percent Fibonacci retracement of the recent fall from 103.20 to 99.06 kicks in.
Others said a wide band of structural resistance could block the contract's way in the 101.10 to 101.20 region.

"The German market has been well underpinned in the last few sessions -- it really didn't want to go down," said a trader. "So when the U.S. market recovered late yesterday, the Bunds had a good reason to push on."
In the cash market the spread between 10-year German and U.S. yields stood at 119 basis points by 0706 GMT, with the 10-year Bund priced at 101.32 for a yield of 5.809 percent.
Analysts said that with Bunds keen to move higher whenever Treasuries were not dragging general sentiment lower, the German market was likely to continue to outclass the U.S. in coming sessions.
